title: Problem-Solving, Ratios, Rates & Data
sub: 20 SPRs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Official Digital SAT Curriculum

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: If \(\frac{9}{2} = \frac{36}{x}\), what is the value of \(x\)?
A quantity \( f_0 = 1800 \) increases by \( 20\% \) to \( f_1 \) and then decreases by \( 25\% \) to \( f_2 \). What is the final quantity \( x = f_2 \)?
If \( \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{36}{x} \), what is the value of \( x \)?
If \( 6 \) identical notebooks cost 66 dollars in total, what is the price per notebook?
A map uses a scale of \(2\) centimeters per \(15\) kilometers. Two towns are \(14\) centimeters apart on the map; how many kilometers apart are they in reality?
In a town of \(4,200\) registered commuters, \(35\%\) travel by train. How many commuters travel by train?
If a car consumes \(9\) liters of fuel to drive \(135\) kilometers, how many liters does it need to travel \(225\) kilometers at the same rate?

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.q: After a \(25\%\) discount, a tablet sells for \(240\) dollars. What was its original retail price in dollars?
A car uses 8 liters of fuel to travel 100 km. How many liters to travel 350 km?
A scatterplot has least-squares regression line \( \hat{f}(x) = 14x + 12 \). What is the predicted value \( \hat{f}(18) \)?
Convert a speed of \(54\) kilometers per hour to meters per second.
The ratio of red beads to blue beads in a jar is \(5 : 8\). If there are \(65\) beads total, how many red beads are in the jar?
A bronze statue has volume \(150\) cubic centimeters and density \(8.4\) grams per cubic centimeter. What is its mass in grams?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(1260\). Mass equals density times volume: \(150 \times 8.4 = 1260\) g.

questions.q: A jacket priced at \(80\) dollars is marked down \(20\%\), and a coupon takes an additional \(15\%\) off the discounted price. What is the final price in dollars?

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: A machine bottles \(180\) jars in \(12\) minutes. At that steady rate, how many jars does it bottle in \(50\) minutes?
A car travels 240 miles in 4 hours. How far in 7 hours?
An orchard harvested \(560\) crates this autumn, which was \(12\%\) more than last autumn. How many crates did it harvest last autumn?
A cyclist rides uphill \(12\) km at \(12\) km/h and returns downhill along the same \(12\) km at \(24\) km/h. What is the average speed in km/h for the entire round trip?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(16\). Total distance \(24\) km divided by total time \((1 + 0.5 = 1.5\text{ hr})\) equals \(16\) km/h.

questions.q: A scatterplot model \(\hat{y} = 3.2x + 14\) predicts sales. If observed sales at \(x = 10\) are \(49\), what is the absolute value of the residual?

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Fluency (21–28)

questions.q: A recipe that serves \(6\) people calls for \(10\) cups of flour. How many cups of flour are needed to serve \(19\) people?
A jacket originally priced at 60 dollars is on sale for 20% off. What is the discount amount in dollars?
If \( x \) is directly proportional to \( y \), and \( x = 14 \) when \( y = 2 \), what is \( x \) when \( y = 5 \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Constant of proportionality \( k = x/y = 14/2 = 7 \). When \( y = 5 \), \( x = 7 \times 5 = 35 \).

questions.q: A recipe requires 2 cups of sugar for every 3 cups of flour. If 9 cups of flour are used, how many cups of sugar are needed?
A survey found that 3 out of every 8 households own a pet. In a neighborhood of 640 households, how many are expected to own a pet?
If \(x\) is directly proportional to \(y\), and \(x = 14\) when \(y = 2\), what is \(x\) when \(y = 5\)?
A store buys backpacks for \(40\) dollars and marks them up by \(35\%\). What is the selling price?
In a recipe, \(3\) cups of oats serve \(5\) people. How many cups of oats are needed for \(35\) people?

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.q: The scatter plot shows the relationship between study hours and scores. Which best describes the correlation?
questions.answer: As study hours increase, scores consistently increase. The points follow a clear upward trend — strong positive correlation.

questions.q: A printer prints 45 pages in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many pages can it print in 8 minutes?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Rate = \( 45 / 3 = 15 \) pages per minute. In 8 minutes: \( 15 \times 8 = 120 \) pages.

questions.q: A cyclist travels at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour. How many miles does the cyclist travel in 3.5 hours?
A class of 30 students has 18 girls and 12 boys. What percentage of the class is boys?
If a team won 21 games and lost 7 games, what fraction of their games did they win?
Population rises from \(16,000\) to \(20,000\) over five years. By what percentage did the population grow?
A line of best fit for electricity bills versus home area (in square feet) is \(\hat{y} = 0.08x + 42\). What does \(0.08\) represent?
choices: Predicted dollar increase per additional square foot
questions.answer: **Answer:** Predicted dollar increase per additional square foot. The slope \(0.08\) gives the predicted change in \(\hat{y}\) (dollars) per \(1\) unit increase in \(x\) (sq ft).

questions.q: How many square inches are in a \(3\)-foot by \(4\)-foot poster (\(1\text{ foot} = 12\text{ inches}\))?
A hybrid sedan travels \(48\) miles per gallon in city traffic. How many gallons of fuel are consumed on a \(216\)-mile trip at that efficiency?

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: An item's price increased from 50 dollars to 65 dollars. What was the percent increase?
A runner completes a 5-kilometer race in 25 minutes. What is the runner's average speed in kilometers per hour?
An electronic device is discounted from 200 dollars to 160 dollars. What is the percent discount?
If 6 workers take 8 days to complete a job, how many days would 12 workers take working at the same pace?
questions.answer: **Answer:** B. Total worker-days = \( 6 \times 8 = 48 \). With 12 workers: \( 48 / 12 = 4 \) days.

questions.q: If \(\frac{a}{15} = \frac{4}{5}\), what is the value of \(a\)?
A store sells notebooks in packs of 5 for 6 dollars. How much would 25 notebooks cost at this rate?
questions.answer: 25 notebooks is 5 packs: 5 dollars \times 6 dollars = 30 dollars$.

questions.q: A price increases by \(20\%\) and is later decreased by \(20\%\). Compared with the starting price, the final price is:
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(4\%\) lower. \(1.20 \times 0.80 = 0.96\), which is \(4\%\) below the starting price.

questions.q: If \(p\) is \(25\%\) greater than \(q\), and \(q\) is \(20\%\) less than \(r\), how does \(p\) compare to \(r\)?
